title: Tsugaru lacquer
summary: Turn a vase, lay coats of dark lac over layers of bright colour, then grind each marked zone with a stone to bring up the mottled colours beneath.
howToPlay: The vase in its frame shows what to make.
Drag across the wood to set its width, then tap the bands to lay the top coat.
Pick a stone and grind each lit zone: a coarse stone cuts deeper.
rules: Shape counts for half the score, the coat on each band for a quarter, and the ground zones for a quarter.
A coarse stone reveals the first layer beneath the coat, a fine stone the next.
Three stars for 88 or more, two stars for 65 and one star for 40. Watch and learn makes a whole piece for you.
heritageNote: Tsugaru lacquerware from Aomori is made from many layers of coloured lac laid over one another and then ground and polished, so that a mottled pattern of bright colours comes up through a dark ground.
